item.title: Codex Memory: AGENTS.md, Memories and Add-ons
item.description:
Codex memory is two built-in layers. AGENTS.md files hold instructions you write, and Codex loads them at the start of every run. Codex memories, off by default, turn useful context from past chats into local files under ~/.codex/memories/. For memory that is searchable, shared across agents or kept on a server, add a hook-based plugin such as Hindsight.

Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent for the terminal, IDE and ChatGPT desktop app. Each session starts with an empty context window, so anything Codex should know must come back in from a file or a tool. Facts below come from OpenAI’s Codex memories docs and AGENTS.md guide, checked 13 October 2026. For Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: AI Coding Agent Memory: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and More
item.description:
AI coding agent memory is how tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot carry project knowledge from one session to the next. The main mechanism is a plain instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or Cursor rules) loaded into every session. Some agents add automatic memory that saves lessons as they work. For more, teams add an external memory server. For Claude Code specifically, see Claude Code memory.

Every session starts with an empty context window, so anything the agent should know about your build, conventions or past mistakes has to be written down somewhere and loaded back. This page compares how the major coding agents do it, from their official docs, checked October 2026.
